It can be hard to balance time between friendships and a relationship, especially when the latter is still new and very exciting. Often it's the friends who get the short end of the stick. But what happens when the significant other is the one who feels robbed?

Have you ever had a friend's SO take a stand over how much time you spend with that friend? Was it treated reasonably, or did jealousy rear its ugly head? What would you do to resolve a situation like that?

Got your own idea for a discussion? Post a thread! /v/relationships welcomes both relationship advice and general discussion questions.
How do you handle the tension of a friend's SO being jealous of your time together?
If your SO is jealous of you spending a reasonable amount of time with other people, it's time to find a new SO.

I just got out of a polyamorous relationship when my paramour found a partner who wanted to be monogamous. They introduced us, we asked if polyamory was an option, and went on hiatus when it got shot down. So not only are we still friends, we've said this is just a break.

Their SO is obviously a bit jealous and uncomfortable when we spend time together. How we've handled it is very open communication and by holding up our agreements. Even when my friend and I are alone together we don't do anything sexual. My friend has asked their SO how they feel and made sure no boundaries have been crossed.

A big part of why this works is how mature, confident, and trusting their SO is. Despite not being completely happy about things, there have been no requests to cut contact and when I last visited their place this person offered me dinner and made me feel welcome. They even allowed my friend and I to go off on the property alone that night, in the dark and away from prying eyes/ears to spend time together.

So I guess the moral of this story is that all parties have to be open and honest as well as refraining from making unreasonable demands. That last item goes both ways: we didn't try to force polyamory or badger them about it later and they didn't try to limit friendship or act like we needed a chaperone.

When we first noticed their jealousy, I made an effort to reach out in friendship to them too and my friend talked with them to make sure their feelings were taken in to account.
